subject: Game Theory
title: Free Rider Problem
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Free Rider Problem.

hook.text: A neighborhood wants a park. Everyone benefits, but nobody wants to pay. The park never gets built.

buildup.text: Free riders enjoy benefits created by others without contributing. Why pay if you get it for free?

discovery.text: Mancur Olson proved large groups suffer more: each person's share is tiny, so nobody feels responsible.

twist.text: Small groups cooperate better because each person matters more and social pressure is stronger.

climax.text: Taxes, unions, and homeowner fees exist because voluntary cooperation fails in large groups.

punchline.text: If everyone waits for someone else, nobody acts.

quiz.question: Why do large groups suffer more from free riding?
